_readme: THE WORDS THE PRESENTATION DOCUMENT POINTS AT.
`docs/presentation/document.md` is the schema. The document carries no rider sentence:
every label and every caption in it is an ID plus the arguments the sentence
interpolates, and this file is where the ids that are not already somewhere else are
resolved. The four other namespaces a `labelId` may use:
glossary.<id>              docs/copy/glossary.json — the nineteen words
tokens.recordWindow.<id>   design/tokens.json recordWindows.order[].label
tokens.layer.<id>          design/tokens.json layers[].label
verdicts.notASession.*     docs/copy/verdicts.json
KIT-OWNED since round 2 of ADR-033: the author is `PresentationCopy` in the kit, which
is what prints these, and this file is the artefact. Regenerate it with
COPY_WRITE=1 swift test --filter CopyContractTests. It was hand-authored here in round
1, which was the right file and the wrong author — the copy contract's rule is that the
kit authors anything the app says (docs/copy/README.md, "The contract").
`label` is the word under the number. `caption` is the small line under a cell, and
carries `{placeholders}` naming the document's own caption arguments. A caption with
a `one` key has a singular form, used when its first argument is 1.
`turnKind` is the rider's word for a kind of sweep, which the wrist-under callout
interpolates; `rowMetric` is the library row's own short spelling of a metric, which
is deliberately shorter than the glossary term because it sits under a value in
caption type beside two others.
`divergence` names the six watch-vs-phone metrics that have no other home — the other
six the check reports are speed records and are named by tokens.recordWindow.<id>.
`banner` is the one sentence the renderer BUILDS rather than names, like turnKind.

caption.fallsSplit: {inTurn} in a turn · {straight} in a straight line
